shortDescription: FuelCell Energy NASDAQ:FCEL falls 0.9% in Tuesday's trading as Citi initiated coverage with a Neutral rating and $19 price target, noting progress towards strategic and financial objectives is picking up pace, with demand from hyperscaler data centers and colocation/neocloud providers driving the o…

children: falls 0.9% in Tuesday's trading as Citi initiated coverage with a Neutral rating and $19 price target, noting progress towards strategic and financial objectives is picking up pace, with demand from hyperscaler data centers and colocation/neocloud providers driving the order pipeline to ~10 GW, and average proposal sizes rising ~3x over the last six months.

The company offers several differentiated strengths, according to Citi's Vikram Bagri, including native DC baseload power, rapid deployment timelines, and more than 20 years of utility-scaleoperating experience, while its molten carbonate platform benefits from a largely U.S.-based supply chain, improved seven-year stack life, better power density, low emissions, chilled-water production, and carbon-capture capabilities.
To leverage the technology and position FuelCell

for long-term success, Bagri said management has implemented recent restructurings that should allow operating expenses to grow roughly in line with inflation while the company benefits from strong operating leverage as it grows production and achieves positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 2027.

product backlog remains modest at ~$109M, and the broader pipeline has yet to convert meaningfully into firm orders, and its ~50% efficiency trails Bloom Energy's SOFC platform, while expanding gas turbine, fuel cell, and engine manufacturing capacity could increase competitive pressure, the analyst said.

title: FuelCell Energy started with Neutral rating at Citi as product backlog remains modest
